questions.question: A 20-something man presents with hyperglycaemia, marked postprandial glucose on OGTT (2-hour 19.8 mmol/L), glycosuria without ketoacidosis, BMI 24.6 kg/m2, negative GAD and IA-2 antibodies, and a family history of early-onset diabetes across three generations. His glucagon-stimulated C-peptide is 0.83 nmol/L. What diagnosis best fits these data and why is it favored over type 1 and type 2 diabetes?
In HNF1A-MODY, why can glycosuria appear at comparatively lower plasma glucose levels, and what renal transporter and transcriptional relationship explain this finding?

List three to five clinical and laboratory clues that should prompt consideration of MODY genetic testing in a young adult with new-onset diabetes, and name one limitation of the commonly used MODY probability calculator in diverse populations.

How do you interpret a glucagon-stimulated C-peptide of 0.83 nmol/L (with a practical threshold of >0.60 nmol/L indicating preserved endogenous insulin), and how should this influence initial therapy when HbA1c is approximately 10% at diagnosis?
What is the first-line pharmacotherapy traditionally recommended for HNF1A-MODY, and under what clinical circumstances might a GLP-1 receptor agonist be preferred?
Why might SGLT2 inhibitors carry disproportionate risks (for example, dehydration and ketoacidosis) in patients with HNF1A-MODY, and how does the disease biology underpin this concern?

Describe the key tissues in which HNF1A is expressed and outline at least two downstream targets or processes relevant to the diabetic phenotype (for example, insulin/GLUT2 expression in β-cells and renal SGLT2 regulation).

In a patient with suspected HNF1A-MODY and severe hyperglycaemia, what is a reasonable sequence of therapy from presentation through stabilization and confirmation of diagnosis, and what factors justify de-escalation off insulin after genetic confirmation?
How would you counsel this patient’s family about inheritance risk, who should be offered testing, and what surveillance is appropriate for relatives found to carry an HNF1A variant?

For a novel missense HNF1A variant (for example, c.809A>G, p.N270S) absent from ClinVar, what ACMG-aligned evidence can support a likely pathogenic classification (consider segregation with disease, location in a critical domain, in silico scores, and phenotype-match), and why is database absence not definitive against pathogenicity?
